brief.title: multinomial: rolling the weighted die for the next token
brief.objective: After watching, the learner can explain that torch.multinomial(probs, num_samples=1) draws one token index at random, weighted by the softmax probabilities, instead of always taking the most likely token, and that the drawn index is appended to the sequence.
brief.audience_context: The learner is in the Attention concept and is looking at the generation loop in GPT.generate (nanoGPT model.py:312-328), where the model's output becomes the next token.
brief.scope_note: 15 seconds covers only the softmax, sample, append step around torch.multinomial. Left out: block_size cropping of the context, the forward pass, temperature scaling, and the details of optional top-k cropping (K1). These are mentioned only as an optional side claim, if at all.

evidence.excerpt:
for _ in range(max_new_tokens):
            # if the sequence context is growing too long we must crop it at block_size
            idx_cond = idx if idx.size(1) <= self.config.block_size else idx[:, -self.config.block_size:]
            # forward the model to get the logits for the index in the sequence
            logits, _ = self(idx_cond)
            # pluck the logits at the final step and scale by desired temperature
            logits = logits[:, -1, :] / temperature
            # optionally crop the logits to only the top k options

# apply softmax to convert logits to (normalized) probabilities
            probs = F.softmax(logits, dim=-1)
            # sample from the distribution
            idx_next = torch.multinomial(probs, num_samples=1)
            # append sampled index to the running sequence and continue
            idx = torch.cat((idx, idx_next), dim=1)

branches.runs: nothing: model.py:320-322 is skipped (no else branch)

claim_registry.text: torch.multinomial(probs, num_samples=1) samples one index from the distribution probs. Each token's chance of being drawn is proportional to its probability, so a less likely token can still be chosen.
probs comes from F.softmax(logits, dim=-1), which turns the final-step logits into normalized probabilities that sum to 1. This happens before sampling.
The sampled index idx_next is appended to the running sequence with torch.cat((idx, idx_next), dim=1), and the loop continues to produce the next token.

Only on the branch where top_k is not None (K1 true), logits below the k-th largest are set to -float('Inf'), so those tokens get zero probability after softmax and cannot be sampled. When top_k is None (K1 false), this step is skipped and every token keeps a nonzero chance.

must_show: A row of logits for the final position becoming a bar chart of probabilities through softmax, with bars that visibly sum to 1
The exact call torch.multinomial(probs, num_samples=1) labeled at the moment of sampling
A weighted random draw that lands on one token, shown at least once landing on a bar that is not the tallest (or with alternate outcomes hinted), so the randomness is clear
Exactly one index (idx_next) coming out of the draw
idx_next being appended to the end of the sequence idx via torch.cat
must_not_claim: That multinomial always picks the highest-probability token (that would be argmax/greedy)
That multinomial returns a probability or a probability vector rather than a token index
That multinomial draws several tokens here (num_samples=1)
That sampling happens before softmax, or that the token is appended before it is sampled (the order is softmax, then multinomial, then torch.cat)
That multinomial modifies or renormalizes probs
That top-k cropping always happens or always removes tokens; it runs only when top_k is not None
That every token always has a nonzero chance; on the top_k branch, cropped tokens have zero probability
brief.visual_direction: Reveal a cause-and-sequence chain left to right. First, focus on the final-position logits turning into probability bars (the transformation). Then focus moves to a weighted chance mechanism over those bars, where wider or taller bars get proportionally more chance, and it settles on one token. A brief ghosted replay can hint that a different bar could have been picked. Finally, the chosen index travels to the end of the token sequence and snaps on, and the eye follows it there to close the loop.
